overview: This bill deals with sterile processing technicians at the Veterans Health Administration, the VA's hospital and clinic system; these workers clean and sterilize surgical tools and medical equipment. It requires people hired into non-entry-level technician jobs to earn a professional certification from an accredited training program within two years. Current technicians who lack certification would have to meet the requirement starting 18 months after the bill becomes law, and the VA must offer them scholarships to earn it. The certification rule expires after September 30, 2028. Separately, the bill extends an existing limit on certain VA pension payments, which applies to some veterans receiving Medicaid-covered nursing home care, from January 31, 2033, to September 30, 2034. As of September 24, 2026, a House committee had approved an amended version and it was awaiting action by the full House.
for: Supporters say requiring certification for the workers who sterilize surgical instruments helps prevent infections in veterans, and paying for current staff to get certified avoids pushing them out.
against: Critics say the requirement could make it harder for VA hospitals to fill these jobs, and that extending the pension payment limit reduces benefits for some veterans in nursing homes.
